app.title: RimWorld Observability
nav.flamegraph.what: One tick drawn as a flame graph. Step through frames and read where the time went.
common.empty.hint: Launch RimWorld with the framework mod to start streaming telemetry.
instrumentation.search.placeholder: Search by type or method name
instrumentation.active.title: Active patches
instrumentation.unavailable: Live instrumentation is unavailable. The game-side library is older than the collector or the control channel has not connected yet.
instrumentation.timeout: The game did not answer in time. Unpause the colony and try again.
instrumentation.failed: The request failed. Check the collector log.
settings.title: Settings
tip.settings.prometheus: When enabled, the collector serves a Prometheus-format /metrics endpoint built from session aggregates.
settings.close_on_disconnect.hint: Close this tab automatically when the collector stops responding (for example, when RimWorld exits). May be blocked by your browser if this tab was not opened by a script.
tip.flamegraph.budget: Budget for one rendered frame. RimWorld's tick loop gives up after 45.45 ms and hands the frame back to rendering, so that is the game's own line for a frame that ran long. It does not move with the speed setting. See Verse.TickManager.TickManagerUpdate.
tip.flamegraph.tickBudget: Budget for one tick at the speed the game is on now, {n}x normal. One frame runs many ticks at higher speeds, so this is the number a single tick has to beat for the game to keep up. The speed is read from the TPS the collector reports, so a game already falling behind can read one speed low.
tip.overview.tps: Ticks per second. RimWorld's simulation clock. Normal speed targets 60 TPS; below 30 indicates the game is struggling to keep up.
tip.overview.fps: Frames rendered per second. Independent of TPS - the game can render smoothly even when the simulation lags.
tip.overview.batches: Total MessagePack telemetry batches received from the library over UDP since the session started.
tip.overview.samples: Total individual samples (timing measurements, metric points, GC events) carried inside those batches.
tip.overview.sections: Number of distinct instrumented code regions currently reporting timings.
tip.overview.gc: Garbage collection events observed since the session started. High counts at gen 2 indicate real memory pressure.
tip.overview.allocations: Estimated allocation events attributed to instrumented sections. Heuristic based on GC.GetTotalMemory deltas.
tip.overview.bytes: Wire bytes received over UDP, before MessagePack decoding.
tip.instrumentation.active: Library has applied the patch and is collecting samples.
tip.instrumentation.pending: Patch was requested but the library has not confirmed it yet.
tip.instrumentation.stale: Library reported the patch was removed or the target method no longer exists.
bundle.export.title: Export a bundle
bundle.export.contentsHint: Manifest, batches, sections, metrics and the report are always included. Tick extras below.
bundle.export.overCapWarning: Over the 25 MB soft cap. Large bundles are slow to share.
bundle.export.forceHint: Override the 25 MB soft cap. Large bundles are slow to share.
comparison.title: Compare sessions
comparison.head: Comparison target
comparison.importHint: Add an exported .rimobs.zip as a comparison source.
comparison.disclaimer: Deltas indicate correlation, not causation. Flagged items are likely regression candidates, not confirmed causes.
comparison.loadOrderNote: Owners are derived from section name prefixes, not the game load order.
comparison.col.head: Head
flamegraph.empty.hint: Launch RimWorld with the framework mod and load a save to start streaming frames.
flamegraph.keys: Arrow keys move between bars, Enter zooms in, Escape fits the whole frame.
flamegraph.source.noFrames: That bundle has no frames.json. Export it again with Frames ticked.
flamegraph.source.emptyFrames: That bundle has an empty frame ring. Nothing was recorded to scrub.
flamegraph.search.label: Find
strip.title: Frame history
flamegraph.keys.transport: Space pauses, PageUp and PageDown step frames, Home jumps to the newest.
tree.col.label: Section
tree.trend.empty: No samples in the last five minutes.
tree.soon: Not collected yet. This tab lights up once its collector ships.
tip.settings.ringCapacity: How many captured frames the strip keeps. The whole buffer ships on every frame poll.
flamegraph.overhead.hint: A floor, not a measurement: scope count times a benchmarked 73.4ns per scope, smoothed once a second. Under auto-instrument the real cost is higher, because filtered and muted scopes still pay entry time that never becomes a node.
tip.tree.patched: Other mods patch this method too. Their timings land inside this section. Patched by:
tip.footer.ring: How many frames the strip holds, out of how many it is configured to hold. Set it in the gear, under Frame buffer.
tip.footer.memory: Process memory is not wired up to the dashboard yet. Nothing to show here until the collector reports it.
tip.footer.timerres: The smallest gap the profiler's clock can tell apart. Every measurement below this floor is noise, not signal.
tip.footer.delta: How much longer or shorter this frame ran than the one before it. A sustained positive delta means the game is falling behind.
flamegraph.keys.title: Keyboard shortcuts
tip.flamegraph.clearRing: Throws away every captured frame the strip is drawing from and starts the history over. The session, its sections and your instrumentation are untouched.
session.name: Name
tip.flamegraph.newSession: Starts a fresh session in the running game, so a long play splits into runs you can name and compare. Entering a game does this on its own.
session.restart.explain: A session is one launch of the game, so starting a new one restarts RimWorld. The name you type is kept and given to the session that comes up next.
session.restart.unsaved: Without a save, anything since your last one is lost.
session.prompt.title: Name this session
session.prompt.explain: A new session just started. Naming it now is what makes it findable later when you compare runs.
tip.settings.autoInstrument: Adds a timing scope to every method your filters match, patching a few milliseconds' worth per frame until it is done. A filter as wide as Assembly-CSharp!* matches over 70,000 methods, which stalls loading for seconds and buries the real hotspots in noise. Start narrow, then widen.
tip.settings.autoInstrument.filters: One pattern per line, in Assembly!Type.Full.Name::Method form. * and ? are wildcards, and a missing assembly or method part means any. Lines starting with # are comments. Leaving this empty instruments nothing.
tip.settings.autoInstrument.ignore: Same pattern form, but these win over the list above no matter what order they are in. Use it to carve hot logging or string-building helpers out of a wide filter, since instrumenting those costs more than they take.
settings.autoInstrument.preview.failed: Could not count. The game may not be running.
settings.autoInstrument.preview.heavy: Wide enough to stall loading for seconds.
tip.settings.autoInstrument.apply: Nothing reaches the game until you press this. The count above is a dry run against the assemblies the game has loaded right now.
settings.autoMuteTrivial: Drop scopes that cost more than they measure
tip.settings.autoMuteTrivial: Removes an instrumented scope once its measured self time never beats the cost of measuring it. Turning this off keeps every scope, which is honest but leaves the call tree full of rows that only show profiler overhead.
tip.settings.maxDepth: How deep nested sections may nest before the library stops recording. Deeper trees fill the sample ring faster, so a high value with auto-instrumentation on can push out the frames you actually wanted. Anything past the cap still runs, it is just not measured.
settings.promptForName: Ask me to name new sessions
tip.settings.promptForName: Shows the naming prompt when a new session starts. Named sessions are the ones you can find again when comparing runs; unnamed ones are only an id and a timestamp.
tip.settings.closeOnDisconnect: Closes this tab when the collector stops answering, which is usually RimWorld exiting. Browsers block this for tabs a script did not open, so it may quietly do nothing.
threads.title: Threads
tip.threads.mainOnly: Draws one lane for the main thread and hides the rest. Turn it off to see Unity job threads and mod threads next to it, which is how you spot work that runs beside the tick loop.
tip.settings.language: Language for the dashboard only. It does not change RimWorld's own language or the section names the game reports.
tip.settings.sessionName: A name for this run. It shows in the session list and in comparisons, so give it something you would recognise next week.
